reading.body:
AutoGPT alone accounts for more than half of the 332,116 combined stars across these four autonomous-agent repositories, making it the dominant public reference point in this space by a wide margin.

The star distribution is heavily skewed. AutoGPT has 187,053 stars, OpenHands has 85,850, gpt-engineer has 55,111, and langroid has 4,102. That spread suggests broad public awareness concentrated at the top, with langroid occupying a narrower, more specialist position. One of the four repositories, gpt-engineer, is archived, meaning active development there has ended and its star count reflects historical interest rather than current momentum.

Three of the four projects are MIT-licensed, which removes legal friction for anyone building on them. The one custom licence belongs to AutoGPT, which may matter to developers evaluating how freely they can fork or embed the code. None of the data here speaks to the compute demands these agents place on infrastructure, beyond the implicit fact that agents that plan and act in loops make repeated model calls, multiplying inference load relative to single-turn queries. The data does not cover deployment scale, API usage, or the power draw of running these systems continuously.
